@mfenniak wrote in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14628/files#issuecomment-24328623:

> `branchMap` is read outside of this lock, which is one lingering concern for me.

I don't follow. `branchMap` is local variable that is handed out to `syncSingleBranch()`, but it is accessed while the lock is held. Have I missed a usage?

A question I have: You're not locking in `syncSingleBranch()`, which is a bit of a maintenance risk. Somebody might come along and reuse `syncSingleBranch()` without realizing that they have to participate in synchronization. It also suggests to me that you do not want to acquire and release the lock for every invocation of `syncSingleBranch()`, but you're doing exactly that. Are interleaving invocations of `syncSingleBranch()` okay or even desired? My intuition would be to hold onto the lock for the entirety of `SyncBranchesToDB()` (or at least for the entire duration of the loop). That ensures that a single invocation has a more or less consistent view of the world.

@aahlenst wrote in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14628#issuecomment-24498987:

> I don't follow. `branchMap` is local variable that is handed out to `syncSingleBranch()`, but it is accessed while the lock is held. Have I missed a usage?

Sorry, I wrote my comment here incorrectly.  You're correct, it is accessed while the lock is held.  It is *initialized* outside of the lock and may contain out-of-date information that doesn't reflect the database state by the time it is used for a logical evaluation.  I think it's safe, but it's a lingering concern for me....

- `branchMap` is created from data that is read at the beginning of the transaction.  Let's say an invocation A reads that branch `main` has commit ID `abc`.
- A concurrent execution of `SyncBranchesToDB` can modify the in-database state of the same branches.  Let's say an invocation B modifies the database, which now reads that the branch `main` has commit ID `def`, and this occurs between invocation A reading the data, and invocation A locking the branch `main`.
- Invocation A now uses out-of-date information in `branchMap` to evaluate the logic [`if ... branch.CommitID == commit.ID.String() ... `](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/b811b26bb7fbd792e5e9627ddaff87c1d59c5377/services/repository/branch.go#L312-L316)
    - I think this is safe; invocation A would read from the git repo that the branch `main` is currently commit `def` (or later), and update the branch because it is not `abc`.
    - The worst-case scenario is that the correct data is already in the DB, but not in-memory, and the `UPDATE` is ineffective.  But an ineffective `UPDATE` is just a very minor inefficiency, in a rare corner case.

---

> A question I have: You're not locking in `syncSingleBranch()`, which is a bit of a maintenance risk. Somebody might come along and reuse `syncSingleBranch()` without realizing that they have to participate in synchronization. 

Originally this was one method.  What I wanted to do is acquire the lock for the specific branch inside the `for` loop, and then release it when the loop is exited.  However, `defer ...` couldn't be used for this because it would release the lock at the end of the *function*, not at the end of each loop.  The logic that is now in `syncSingleBranch` has 8 exit points, so I didn't want to have 8 lock release points within the for loop.

The solution was to move it to a separate method so that I could have a single lock and unlock point.

But, I agree with you that it creates a risk for future users of `syncSingleBranch` that I didn't identify.  Now that it is in a separate method, the lock acquisition can also be moved into `syncSingleBranch`, a `defer` can be used to unlock once, and that eliminates the maintenance risk as well.  That fix is now in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/compare/b811b26bb7fbd792e5e9627ddaff87c1d59c5377..6fd4741020b02613be7815b208581b84ec8db625. 👍

> It also suggests to me that you do not want to acquire and release the lock for every invocation of `syncSingleBranch()`, but you're doing exactly that. Are interleaving invocations of `syncSingleBranch()` okay or even desired?

It is OK & desired, as long as they are separate branches.

> My intuition would be to hold onto the lock for the entirety of `SyncBranchesToDB()` (or at least for the entire duration of the loop). That ensures that a single invocation has a more or less consistent view of the world.

This would require either elevating the lock to a repository-level lock (rather than branch-level), or, managing the risk of deadlocks between branches.  If two pushes are received, one for `{branch-a, branch-b}`, and one for `{branch-b, branch-a}`, they could both acquire a lock on the first branch, and be unable to acquire a lock on the second because it is held by the other invocation.
